title: Residual coverage manifest for the open oriented claims at G = 75 (AES MixColumns 75-gate proof framework)
status_of_everything_here: LP / MILP status [measured] with the published combined rows (sprint Addenda A-D + October push5/push6); not certificates. The lower bound stays 75.

definitions.claim: an oriented claim (scalar state, orientation) of the package's final test at G = 75; open iff k <= Se, l <= So and k + l <= budget with k, l the least LP-feasible levels of the even and odd phase keys
definitions.key: (h, y, F, orientation, q, z): a local linear system on helper type counts (r, u, v); level s = q + z
definitions.leaf: (A = a, q_D = d): the exact hub case (a = number of full-met missing labels) and dark case (d = number of dark missing labels) of a key's case tree; a key is excluded iff every leaf is
definitions.ladder: for a claim, the LP-feasible keys at every level that could keep it open (even: le <= s <= min(Se, budget - lo); odd: lo <= s <= min(So, budget - le)); the 229 'load-bearing' keys are the first-level keys only

hypotheses.A01_or_dark: every leaf with A >= 2 and q_D = 0 excluded
hypotheses.INT: every integer-infeasible leaf certified (type counts are integers)

explanations.concentrated_vs_covered: 'The open leaves are concentrated at A = 2..4 with no dark label' is a statement about the 572 first-layer leaves (380 have A in 2..4, 481 have q_D = 0). 'All remaining claims are covered by that region' would require every claim to die once those leaves are excluded. It is false: excluding every leaf with A >= 2 leaves 119 claims open (driver scan; the ladder evaluation gives the per-claim list), because 62 of the 229 first-layer keys have an open leaf with A <= 1 and further keys behind the first layer take over. Excluding every leaf with A >= 1 still leaves 88 claims open on A = 0 configurations, where no hub argument applies.
explanations.old_enumerations: The sprint's two unrun enumerations (M^T q = 1 with 7-8 full helpers; M q = 2 with ten) address no live obligation: no key with q <= 2 is in any ladder's first layer, the sprint's q = 1 representatives (19,0,0,Mt,1,5), (18,1,1,Mt,1,4), (12,5,1,Mt,1,4), (11,7,1,Mt,1,4) are LP-infeasible under the combined rows, and the 82 LP-feasible q <= 2 keys appear only behind the first layer (listed in the ladders where they do). They are removed from the immediate task.
explanations.the_101_keys: The 101 keys the sprint's MILP oracle classified integer-infeasible (20 s limit, status not recorded) were never used as exclusions: the 280 count is LP status. None of them is a first-layer key today; one, (11,7,0,M,4,2), is LP-feasible behind the first layer. Their classification stays unresolved; today's leaf survey (status recorded, all solves terminated with status 0 or 2) is a separate measurement and also not a certificate.
explanations.pairwise_sharing: Finite GF(2) rank check (share_pairs.py): anchored hubs with no full-met label CAN share a hub-only label with the Lemma-J family independent (M: 361,168 / 58,172 / 3,900 mask pairs for classes r = 1/1, 1/2, 2/2; M^T: 481,440 / 83,940 / 5,748). So no per-pair finite fact yields a row; remaining obstructions are joint over whole configurations.
